target_customer: Seniors choosing Medicare plans (consumer side), later Medicare carriers and brokerages buying AI voice agents
problem: Seniors found Medicare enrollment confusing, and traditional brokers favored plans paying the highest commissions.
business_model: Licensed insurance brokerage earning carrier commissions, later B2B AI software for carriers and brokerages
product_category: Medicare brokerage and AI insurance agent

founders.name: Daniel Petkevich
founders.background_notes: The press release says he built the brokerage after watching his parents go through Medicare enrollment. A search snippet calls him the technical co-founder of Trim, not verified from an opened source.

competitors.name: SelectQuote
competitors.what: Telephone and online distributor of Medicare Advantage and other insurance, commission based

competitors.name: GoHealth
competitors.what: Online Medicare plan broker earning carrier commissions
competitors.traction_then: about 10 percent of Medicare Advantage sign-ups in 2019 per a search result
competitors.funding_then: IPO raised about 914 million dollars in July 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Plan ranking algorithms and a benefits web portal plus a licensed brokerage operation. The hard parts were licensing and operations, not technology, until the later AI voice products.

defensibility.rationale: Broker licences in all states are a hurdle but existing brokers hold them already, and the commission agnostic positioning is easy to claim.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large brokers did not copy the pitch directly; the Department of Justice later sued eHealth, GoHealth and SelectQuote over kickback allegations, per 2025 news results.

market_need_then: The 2022 release cites broker churn above 40 percent and an average broker net promoter score of 34 in 2021, and says brokers favor high commission plans.

branding.name_origin: Fair Square suggests fair dealing and commission agnostic advice; the company states it focuses on educating instead of selling. No source states the origin of Vox.

rebrands.why: Rebrand tied to the Vox AI platform for carriers and brokerages introduced in 2024-08; the exact rename date and rationale were not found

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage of the brand is mostly funding and product news. No evidence of community or distinctive brand assets was found.

pivots.to: AI voice agents and generative AI tools for Medicare carriers and brokers (Vox)
pivots.why: Sourced to coverage of the Vox launch; the company's own reason was not found

outcome_analysis: Fair Square started as a commission agnostic Medicare brokerage out of YC W20 and raised a 15 million dollar Series A in 2022, with about 19 million stated as total raised. In 2024 it pivoted toward selling AI voice tools to carriers and brokers under the Medicare Vox name. A single aggregator reports a sale to Senior Market Sales in January 2026, which is unconfirmed.
notes: Total raised is about 19 million per the press release, so roughly 4 million predates the Series A; searches found no seed round announcement. An acquisition by Senior Market Sales dated 2026-01-30 appears in PitchBook and Seedtable snippets only, so exit is recorded as none, matching the Active status on YC. Founding year is 2019 on YC and 2020 in press. Competitors are listed from 2020 dated sources; they were not named in the company's own materials. Headquarters differs across sources. The company site returned a 503 error.
